about: Count gate (PLAN-4.5 §3), checked by scripts/perf-gate.mjs in `npm test`. A metric fails when its value is above its limit. Limits may only go down: each PLAN-4.5 workstream lowers the ones it improves when it lands. `baseline` is the value measured when the limit was last set (`tolerance`: how far below it counts as an improvement). Exact limits for the counts, which repeat exactly (the select-row patch count can drop to 1,000 under CPU load, when two 1 ms render debounces coalesce; it never exceeds 1,001, one patch per item plus the parent); headroom only for the setTimeout count (81,000) and the heap, as proposed in dev-plans/research/p45-perf-baseline.md §5. P45-A: ScopeCheckers 5,000 → 1 (the one left is G-252, the first instance kept by the shared INITIALIZE reducer), heap 8.76 → 1.17 MB (limit 1.5). P45-B: streams 151 → 149/item, unmount setTimeouts 79,013 → 77,013 (limit 79,000), ScopeCheckers 0 (G-252 fixed), heap 1.02 MB. P45-C (one scheduler per app): patches 1 / 1 / 1 (one patch per flush; exact), streams 122/item, unmount setTimeouts 70,013 (limit 71,000). P45-D (lazy wiring, synchronous teardown): streams 22/item, unmount setTimeouts 9 (limit 100: one timer per teardown level plus start timers), heap 0.95 MB (limit 1.2).
